items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: We were listening – we weren’t doing that thing of like you can’t walk until you learn to crawl. A lot of us were listening to Ornette Coleman and Clifford Brown and Charlie Parker...

ctx.x: Did you get the – early on the idea of, I’ll call it the typical jazz performance where the head is at the beginning and at the end. And in the middle there’s this as long as it goes. But still with structure. Did that dawn on you by yourself or did you have help from a teacher?

Good question. Well I was just listening and listening and listening so much that – but what was unique perhaps for me or my age, those kids that were like in high school in the mid-‘70s. I was high school class of ’75. We were listening – we weren’t doing that thing of like you can’t walk until you learn to crawl. A lot of us were listening to Ornette Coleman and Clifford Brown and Charlie Parker and very quickly and Anthony Braxton and Roscoe Mitchell and – so music that would be considered more quote straight…
Did Chick Corea and his electric band or Weather Report have a space in there somewhere?
